item.title: Why local-first software feels different
item.dc:creator: Avery Lin
item.description: Ownership of data changes the shape of the product: no sync spinner, no outage page.
item.content:encoded:
Ownership of data changes the shape of the product: no sync spinner, no outage page.

When the database lives in the browser, a feed refresh is a local transaction. That single constraint removes an entire category of failure — and with it, an entire category of UI. There is no "reconnecting" banner, no retry counter, no partial write you have to reconcile later. The trade is obvious: your data does not follow you between devices unless you export it yourself.

Local-first is a promise about who owns the write.

For a reader, that promise is the whole point: the list of things you meant to read is small, personal, and nobody else's business.

  • No account
  • No telemetry
  • No ranking
